headline: GOLD CRATERS ANOTHER 3.71% TO $3,530 TODAY — Deepens Correction From Aug ATH; $3,500 Structural Support Level Now in Sight
snippet: Spot gold fell a further 3.71% to $3,530.75 on November 20, extending the multi-week correction from August all-time highs in what analysts are describing as a broad metals and equity selloff driven by hawkish US rate expectations — gold opened the day at $3,730 on COMEX and by mid-session had shed nearly $200 as dollar strength and speculative de-leveraging hit the complex simultaneously. The $3,500 zone is now the next critical test: multiple central bank accumulation programs are widely expected to activate sustained buying at or below that level, and a close through it would mark gold's lowest price in 15 months — a threshold that could accelerate forced liquidation in leveraged mining equity positions before longer-term buyers step in.

headline: TRUMP VOWS TO 'CATCH CHINA' ON RARE EARTHS — USAR +5%, MP Materials +3% as Policy Backstop Narrative Revives Beaten Sector
snippet: President Trump's public pledge on November 19 to 'catch China' on rare earth production and processing drove USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) up 5% and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) up 3% — the third distinct rally trigger for the sector in a week, following the APEC-week Trump-Xi meeting and a session of US-China trade talks on rare earth supply chains. The critical question the analysis raises is whether successive policy backstop signals can sustain a sector still down 30-40% from 2026 peaks while structural feedstock challenges — specifically the William Blair downgrade concern about USAR's processing capacity — remain unresolved; for retail investors, the gap between political narrative and project-level fundamentals is the core risk in deciding how much of these bounce moves to participate in versus wait for firmer operational data.

headline: FOREMOST CLEAN ENERGY DISCOVERS URANIUM AT TURKEY LAKE ONTARIO — Inaugural Drill Program Hits Mineralization; Chemical Assays Pending on 5 Holes
snippet: Foremost Clean Energy (TSX-V) announced a uranium mineralization discovery during its inaugural drill program at the Turkey Lake Project in Ontario on November 17, with radiometric survey results confirming uranium-bearing intervals across multiple drill holes and chemical assay results pending — the company is drilling in a region of Ontario that has historically hosted uranium deposits associated with the uranium-rich Precambrian basement geology that underpins the Athabasca Basin's southern margins. While grades are unconfirmed until chemical results return, the discovery of mineralization in the first drill campaign establishes Turkey Lake as a live exploration target and places Foremost alongside a small group of TSX-V uranium developers adding new project inventory at a moment when uranium miner equities have significantly lagged spot uranium price performance.

headline: GLOBAL ENERGY METALS CLOCKS 37,265 CPS URANIUM ANOMALY IN SASK — Charlot-Neely Lake Radiometric Results Hit Project Record
snippet: Global Energy Metals (TSX-V: GEMC) reported highly anomalous uranium radioactivity results of up to 37,265 counts per second at its Charlot-Neely Lake project in Saskatchewan on November 18 — the highest radiometric reading recorded on the property to date — from a ground-based radiometric survey expanding the known uranium-bearing footprint. The Saskatchewan uranium district has attracted renewed institutional attention as nuclear energy's role in AI data centre power and national energy security strategies grows; Charlot-Neely Lake's proximity to established infrastructure and the project's expanding radiometric anomaly position it as a development-stage uranium target among TSX-V investors looking for leverage to uranium's long-term supply thesis at a time when miner equities are historically cheap relative to spot.

headline: US-CHINA RARE EARTH TALKS SEND WHOLE SECTOR SURGING — USAR +7%, MP Materials +8%, United States Antimony +7% in One Session
snippet: Rare earth equities surged across the board on November 18 as traders positioned for US-China bilateral talks on rare earth supply chains, with USA Rare Earth up 7%, MP Materials up 8%, and United States Antimony up 7% in the session — the kind of broad sector lift that typically reflects institutional short-covering alongside retail momentum buying rather than any individual company catalyst. China's October 2025 rare earth export controls remain in effect under a licensing regime despite Beijing's pause on further escalation, meaning any thaw in US-China rare earth trade talks would directly address one of the sector's key overhang risks; the two-day consecutive gains also partially reversed the sector's steep post-APEC profit-taking and William Blair downgrade selloff from earlier in the week.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE SLIDES 6% TO CAD $232 TODAY — Can Record Gold Production Prevent Further Downside as Sector Selloff Deepens?
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX: AEM) fell approximately 6% to CAD $232 on November 20 as the gold sector selloff intensified, with lower commodity prices and rising mining expenditure combining to pressure profitability metrics even as the company's operational performance remains strong — Agnico's production figures for 2026 are tracking near record levels, creating an unusual situation where fundamentals are improving while equity prices are deteriorating. The disconnect illustrates the core challenge for retail investors evaluating senior gold producers right now: operational strength is not translating to stock price support as macro headwinds — a strengthening dollar, hawkish Fed expectations, and broad risk-off selling — override company-specific fundamentals in a way that historically resolves when the macro environment stabilises.

headline: URANIUM MINERS DOWN 31% WHILE SPOT GAINS 10% IN 2026 — Investor Analysis Flags Historic Equity-Spot Disconnect as Entry Setup
snippet: An investor analysis published in November 2026 examines why URNM — the leading uranium mining ETF — is down approximately 31% year-to-date even as the spot uranium price has gained roughly 10% over the same period, attributing the divergence primarily to cost inflation hitting mining margins, speculative position unwinds from the 2024-2025 uranium equity mania, and broader risk-off selling that has treated uranium miners as high-beta cyclicals rather than energy-transition infrastructure proxies. The historical precedent the analysis cites is the 2016-2018 uranium cycle, when a similar equity-spot divergence persisted for 12-18 months before resolving sharply higher as spot finally pulled mining equities up; the note concludes that investors who correctly time the re-rating would need a catalyst — a utility contracting wave, a supply disruption, or a regulatory tailwind — rather than simply waiting for spot strength alone to lift equities.

headline: SOARING CHINA COPPER PREMIUMS PULL US PHYSICAL METAL EAST — Yangshan at Record $360/t While LME Futures Continue Slide
snippet: Soaring Yangshan copper import premiums — reportedly at a record $360 per tonne — are drawing physical copper out of US warehouses toward Asia despite LME copper futures continuing to slide, according to market sources cited by Mining.com, illustrating the stark divergence between the financial and physical copper markets that experienced cycle investors use to identify approaching bottoms. The physical premium surge signals that Chinese end-users are paying up for actual copper at the same time that speculative and AI-demand-unwinding selling is driving financial copper lower — a pattern that in previous cycles has preceded sharp recoveries once futures positioning normalises and physical market reality reasserts itself through the LME's pricing mechanism.

headline: GEIGER COUNTER TRUST NOTES 'GROWING URANIUM DEMAND' — Nuclear Investment Pace Accelerating; UK Trust Flags Spot Above $91/lb as Structural Inflection
snippet: Kepler Trust Intelligence's November 2026 note on the Geiger Counter uranium fund described the recent pullback in uranium mining shares as a possible entry point, with the spot price holding above US$91 per pound — a level the fund manager associates with the threshold where new primary uranium supply economics work and where utility buyers historically begin contracting. The fund's view that nuclear investment is accelerating globally — driven by AI data centre power demand, grid decarbonisation policy, and small modular reactor development commitments from the US, UK, and several Asian nations — provides a structural demand argument that is distinct from the financial market volatility pressuring uranium miner equities, and positions the current equity weakness as an opportunity rather than a thesis change for investors with a 3-5 year horizon.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL: 3 CRITICAL MINERAL STOCKS COULD MAKE INVESTORS A FORTUNE BY 2035 — Names Top Battery Metals Picks for Long-Horizon Accounts
snippet: Motley Fool's November 19 screen for critical mineral stocks with decade-long return potential highlights three names with exposure to the battery metals and energy transition supply chains, applying a methodology that filters for balance sheet strength, proven resource base, and management execution track records rather than just commodity price leverage — criteria designed to identify companies that can navigate one or more commodity cycles rather than depending on perfect timing. For retail investors evaluating battery metals exposure in a year when lithium stocks are significantly down and copper equities have sold off from AI-demand highs, the analysis provides a framework for distinguishing between high-quality development assets in temporarily depressed sectors versus speculative names riding a thesis without the operational fundamentals to survive an extended downturn.

headline: THESE JUNIOR MINERS DEFIED THE 2026 BEAR MARKET — Stockhead Names ASX Explorers Bucking the Sector Selloff
snippet: Stockhead's analysis identifies a small cohort of ASX junior mining companies that have held or grown their market caps through the 2026 junior mining bear market — a period in which the broader TSX-V and ASX small-cap mining sectors declined sharply as gold corrected from all-time highs, lithium prices remained depressed, and risk-off sentiment compressed junior exploration valuations. The common threads among the outperformers, according to the analysis, are exceptional drill results with grades and widths above peer averages, tight share structures that prevented warrant-related dilution, and projects in established mining jurisdictions where infrastructure lowers the bar to development — criteria that experienced junior mining investors cite as the durable fundamentals that separate real discoveries from exploration stories dressed up by commodity cycle momentum.
